sources.title: Llama-2-7b-chat-hf official model card and license
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the exact repository identifies the dialogue-optimized 7B fine-tuned model. Meta describes SFT/RLHF, text input/output, 4k context, and the Llama 2 Community License.

sources.title: Meta and Microsoft Introduce the Next Generation of Llama
sources.evidence: Dated July 18, 2023; announces availability of pretrained and conversationally fine-tuned Llama 2 weights and code that day.

sources.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: Section 1 explicitly releases 7B Llama 2-Chat as a fine-tuned Llama 2 variant. Sections 3.2.3, 3.3 and 4.2.4 describe tuning on 70B-generated responses, Ghost Attention training-data changes and safety context distillation, not architectural compression. Table 1 and Appendix A.2.1 specify 7B, no GQA and 4096 tokens; Section 5.1 discusses prompted tool use.

sources.title: Llama 2 original model card, llama_v2 branch
sources.evidence: Lists released 7B pretrained and fine-tuned variants, nominal parameter classes, text modalities, custom commercial licensing, and the GQA distinction for 70B.

sources.title: Llama 2 original Transformer implementation
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the shared released Transformer uses causal attention, dense SwiGLU feed-forward layers, RMSNorm and rotary positions. No expert router or Chat-specific structural branch is present; absent n_kv_heads defaults to n_heads (MHA).

sources.title: Llama 2 original generation implementation
sources.evidence: The released interface accepts system/user/assistant text and produces assistant text. It exposes no dedicated reasoning channel, reasoning-budget control, tools argument, or tool-message protocol.

sources.title: Public metadata for Meta Llama-2-7b-chat-hf
sources.publisher: Hugging Face metadata for Meta repository
sources.evidence: Re-fetched October 27 via the public API: manual gating and 6,738,417,664 F16 safetensors elements remain reported, with lastModified April 17, 2024. Storage-element metadata is not used as a learned-weight census or an active-count definition.

sources.title: Exact variant configuration access attempt
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 browser access again failed for this gated file. No authentication bypass or weight download was attempted; access is unnecessary to retain the published nominal specification.

sources.title: Mixtral of Experts, Section 3 Table 2
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27: the original benchmark Table 2 explicitly lists LLaMA 2 7B with 7B under Active Params. This is Mistral's nominal comparison convention for the base model, not a Meta active-count disclosure or an exact Chat-checkpoint census.

sources.title: Current Meta llama-models Llama 2 model card
sources.evidence: Freshly located and opened October 27: retains the 7B/13B/70B pretrained and fine-tuned variants, SFT/RLHF lineage and explicit 7B Llama-2-Chat evaluation row. No replacement count or structural change is specified.

name.note: Readable name for the exact 7B dialogue-tuned repository.

release_date.note: Original public release of the family including the 7B Chat variant; not a later hosting date.

open_weights.note: Weights were released under a custom license; current access requires accepting Meta conditions.

license.note: Custom license, not an Apache or MIT license.

parameters_b.note: Meta explicitly publishes 7B for the exact Chat fine-tune; retain this nominal specification. The fresh current card and original paper agree. No exact learned-weight census is claimed or required.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal inference: Mistral's original Mixtral Table 2 explicitly reports 7B Active Params for Llama 2 7B base. Apply that convention to Meta's explicitly named 7B Chat fine-tune. The paper describes SFT/RLHF; its generated-response/context distillation supplies tuning data rather than compressing the 7B architecture. No pruning, expert expansion or added modality is documented. This is a lineage inference using Mistral's research comparison, not a Chat-specific active-count disclosure from Meta or exact per-token tensor participation.

architecture.note: Dense autoregressive Transformer with SwiGLU and ordinary MHA. The 7B row excludes GQA; the larger-model GQA specification must not be transferred.

context_window.note: Trained context: 4096 tokens, explicit in Appendix A.2.1 and consistent with Chat SFT sequence length.

modalities.note: Text-only input and output are explicit.

reasoning.note: No dedicated reasoning mode or channel is specified. Reasoning tasks and prompted explanations do not establish this capability flag.

tool_call.note: Family-level prompted tool-use experiments do not verify native structured tool calling for the exact 7B variant; original interface has no tool protocol.

description.note: Accurate: dialogue tuning used SFT and RLHF.

patch.notes: Meta publishes a nominal 7B total for this Chat fine-tune. Nominal 7B active is inferred through its documented Llama 2 7B lineage using Mistral's Mixtral Table 2 active-count convention; Meta does not separately disclose a Chat active count. Exact per-token tensor participation is unspecified. Dense MHA architecture and a 4096-token trained context are documented. Dedicated reasoning and native tool-calling interfaces are not established.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains Meta's nominal 7B total and establishes nominal 7B active by combining Mistral's explicit base-model comparison with Meta's Chat fine-tuning lineage. Reopened original sources and searched current Meta cards; no contradictory structural change or more precise Chat active disclosure found. Exact tensor participation remains unspecified. All twelve nonparameter assessments are preserved.
